domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Postoperative pain was evaluated using a visual analogue scale (VAS 0: no pain, 10 cm: worst pain ever) with 15 min intervals in PACU (0h.), then at postoperative 2., 4., 6., 8., 12., 18., 24., and 48. hours at the ward by a research assistant who was blinded to the study groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT04193488), and reported all pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes according to the planned analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered with the Clinical Trials.gov (NCT04193488)... Primary outcome measure was mean pain scores. Secondary outcome measures were consumption of opioid rescue analgesic and the amount of analgesic which was delivered by the patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) in the postoperative period.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to domain 1, because the method of random sequence generation was not specified despite the use of sealed opaque envelopes for allocation concealment. All other domains had low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study is a prospective randomized controlled trial where eligible patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to either the erector spinae plane block group or the control group using a random number table generated via www.randomization.com.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random sequence was used with allocation concealment via opaque envelopes opened just before anesthesia, and baseline characteristics were comparable between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomized (1:1) and divided into a control group (Group C; n = 40) and an ultrasound-guided ESPB group (Group ESP; n = 40) by the random number table method (www.randomization.com) (Fig. 1). The randomized schedule was hidden and generated by the anesthesiologist in charge of the case, who was not part of the study. The same anesthesiologist prepared the envelopes, and the envelopes were opened just before anesthesia.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention was administered under general anesthesia, intraoperative care was standardized and administered by blinded anesthesiologists, and deviations from intended interventions were minimal and balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In Group ESP, the patients underwent ultrasound-guided ESPB under general anesthesia before surgery, while Group C was set as blank control group without ESPB... All patients underwent standardized general anesthesia at our hospital by two anesthesiologists who were blinded to group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were available for all 40 patients analyzed per group out of 86 randomized, with post-randomization exclusions (pre-specified surgical conversion/mechanical ventilation criteria) being balanced (3 in ESP, 3 in Control) and unlikely to bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Following randomization, five patients were excluded because they underwent thoracotomy, and one patient was excluded due to the need for postoperative mechanical ventilation. Therefore, we analyzed the results of 40 patients in each group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were blinded to group allocation, and postoperative opioid consumption was recorded objectively via a PCA device.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The collection of all the data was performed by the same anesthesiologist who unaware of the patients’ details and grouping, but who was familiar with the assessment methods and indices used in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, and the reported primary and secondary outcomes align with the pre-specified protocol without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered prior to patient enrollment at chictr.org.cn (identifier: ChiCTR1900022217).

overall_summary: The trial was well-designed and conducted with adequate random sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding of care providers and outcome assessors, minimal and balanced exclusions, and prospective registration, resulting in a low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the ESP group or control group using a computer-generated random sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed in sealed envelopes opened in the operating room, and baseline characteristics were comparable between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly chosen to receive either ESP plus conventional opioid analgesics (group ESP, n = 30) or receive only the conventional opioid analgesics (group C, n = 30) by a random sequence number generated by the computer kept in sealed envelopes. The sealed envelopes will be opened on the day of surgery when the patient in the operation room and participants will receive either ESP or not as per the envelope.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although patients were not blinded (no sham block), interventions were delivered per protocol prior to general anaesthesia, standardized multimodal background analgesia and strict rescue protocols were applied, and all randomized participants were analyzed according to assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: First, it was only a single-blinded study. No other block group was established, which may be considered a limitation. Since patients know whether or not they have received an injection for ESP block, the placebo effect could not be minimized.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 60 randomized participants (30 per group) completed the study and had complete outcome data available for analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The remaining 60 patients were allocated equally into two groups: ESP (study) group and C (control) group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the postoperative observer was blinded, patients were not blinded to receiving the block intervention, which could influence patient-reported outcomes like VAS pain scores and patient-requested rescue morphine.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The observer anaesthesiologist postoperative will be blinded to which group the patient belongs.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, and the reported primary (morphine consumption) and secondary outcomes correspond with the pre-specified plan without signs of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was registered on Clinical-Trials.gov and was assigned an NCT number, Clinical-Trials.gov ID NCT03749395.

overall_summary: The study had an overall judgment of some concerns due to potential bias in outcome measurement: patients were aware of their treatment assignment (lack of a sham control procedure), which may have influenced subjective pain scores and subsequent morphine consumption despite blinding of the postoperative observer.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the block group or the control group using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed using opaque envelopes until assignment, and baseline characteristics were broadly balanced except for an age difference consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were allocated to either block group (group B) or control group (group C) using computer‑generated random numbers. Random numbers were concealed using opaque envelopes and were opened just prior to the administration of block.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and proceduralists were unblinded (no sham procedure was performed in the control group), which could lead to deviations from the intended protocol or differential care, although standard intraoperative and postoperative protocols were specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The anesthetist who performed the block was not blinded to group allocation... Second, the patient and the anesthetist performing the block were not blinded to the group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 60 randomized patients (30 in each group) were followed up and included in the final analysis with no missing outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 65 patients undergoing total mastectomy and axillary clearance were assessed for eligibility, out of 5 were excluded and 60 patients were randomized into two groups [Figure 1]. Both the groups were comparable... [and all 30 per group were analyzed].

domain_judgments.rationale: Postoperative pain scores were recorded by an investigator blinded to the study, and morphine consumption was recorded objectively via an IV PCA device.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The pain score on a numeric rating scale (NRS) was recorded at 0, ½, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 24 h by an investigator blinded to the study... An intravenous patient‑controlled analgesia (PCA) pump was used to provide morphine for rescue analgesia in all the patients

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a prospective trial registry identifier or pre-published statistical analysis plan, raising some concerns for potential selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 24‑hour morphine consumption was considered as the primary outcome and secondary outcomes included time to first rescue analgesia, pain scores at 0, ½, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 24 h and characteristics and complications associated with block procedure.

overall_summary: The study has an overall judgment of some concerns due to lack of participant blinding (no sham intervention) and lack of evidence of prospective trial registration or a pre-published statistical analysis plan, despite adequate randomization concealment, blinded outcome assessment, and complete follow-up.
